newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Zimbabwe to introduce value-added tax in 1998.
newsitem.headline: Zimbabwe to introduce value-added tax in 1998.

text.p: Zimbabwe would introduce value-added tax (VAT) in 1998 in an effort to boost its revenue collection, Finance Minister Herbert Murerwa said in his national budget speech on Thursday.
He said in his 1997/98 budget speech that Zimbabwe's current tax collection system left out a number of potential tax payers, resulting in low funds to the government.
He gave no specific timeframe for the introduction of the new tax.
The new budget runs for 18 months from this month to December 1998 to allow Zimbabwe to convert its financial year to a calender year in 1998.
Earlier this year, Murerwa launched a blitz on tax evaders which raked in millions of dollars for the government.
